title: Evidence blobs and connector-owned sync positions

nodes.summary: Captured bytes use a nominal SDK BlobRef stored per instance
nodes.detail: BlobRef (sha256, size, mediaType, name) is a recognised nominal SDK type found by schema inspection through nested contracts, never inferred from similar records. Bytes live under the instance's evidence directory as blobs/<sha256>, and payloads hold references, not bytes or paths, with instance-local dedup only.
sections: Decision / Captured bytes have typed references

realised.evidence: PR #215 adds the nominal SDK BlobRef, found by nominal contract walk (blobReferences), stored per instance under blobs/<sha256>

nodes.summary: Blob downloads stream through the host, never into guest
nodes.detail: Acquisition gains StoreBlob, which the native interpreter streams to a temp file while hashing, returning a BlobResponse with HTTP status/headers so plugins can handle 429/503 and Retry-After; only complete downloads yield a reference, with no hidden retries and no guest-memory bytes.
sections: Decision / Acquisition streams through the host

nodes.summary: Blob reads confined to references in one captured snapshot
nodes.detail: readBlob/readBlobText are CapturedRead effects resolvable only for references reachable in the invocation's EvidenceSnapshot; missing or corrupt bytes are errors, never a provider refetch, and a known hash is not a historical-read API.
sections: Decision / Reads belong to one captured invocation

realised.evidence: PR #215: CapturedRead = EvidenceRead :+: BlobRead; the broker rejects references outside the captured input, and missing/corrupt bytes are errors with refetch guidance

nodes.summary: Blobs complete before atomic publish; unreferenced bytes reclaimed safely
nodes.detail: Publication verifies every reference resolves to a complete blob before the atomic state replacement, and commits evidence, markers and position together. Afterwards bytes not referenced by Available payloads are reclaimed, and a host-only BlobScope protects in-flight readers and downloads across processes.

nodes.summary: CLI/MCP results attach read-only local file paths to BlobRefs
nodes.detail: At presentation the host finds BlobRefs via the checked result contract and supplies a read-only path to the captured local blob from the originating instance. Kyyn adds no PDF, OCR or conversion engine and keeps no second archive.
sections: Decision / Surface results expose files, not binary transcripts

realised.evidence: PR #215: CLI/composed-tool method results resolve BlobRefs via the checked contract and list each blob's local path; no file-mode read-only enforcement found, MCP path not separately evidenced

nodes.summary: Typed connector sync positions persist atomically with evidence
nodes.detail: Stateful fetch takes a FetchContext (host startedAt instant and prior position) and returns a FetchResult with a plugin-defined Position type checked by the compiler. The host stores it in the state document beside evidence and advances it only on successful publication. Pagination/reset logic is plugin-owned and positions never feed history, citations or recipe progress.
sections: Decision / Sync positions are typed connector data

realised.evidence: PR #203 infers typed FetchContext/FetchResult from connector signatures and publishes evidence plus Dhall position atomically

nodes.summary: Positions survive source config changes; clear the instance to restart
nodes.detail: Only changed code or contract invalidates a stored position. A source configuration change continues the prior sync, and an agent explicitly clears the instance's evidence and position to start fresh, with no config-identity mechanism.
sections: Decision / Sync positions are typed connector data

realised.evidence: PR #203: 'Configuration has no new identity mechanism: agents explicitly clear an instance to restart'

nodes.summary: --restart-sync withholds the position once, retaining evidence
nodes.detail: evidence fetch --restart-sync passes Nothing once while keeping evidence for comparison; evidence clear deletes evidence and position; for stateless connectors restart is a reported no-op.
sections: Decision / Sync positions are typed connector data

realised.evidence: PR #204 implements generic --restart-sync and Calendar delta on typed positions

nodes.summary: Host-streamed blob downloads with no size or media-type policy
nodes.detail: Downloads still stream through the host to a hashed temporary file, and only complete downloads yield a reference (the surviving core of 0029.02). BlobDownload drops maxBytes, so there is no connector size limit or media-type skip policy: a download either completes or fails the acquisition.
sections: Decision / Acquisition streams through the host

realised.evidence: PR #215 streams downloads natively to a hashed temporary file and renames only complete downloads; BlobDownload has no size or media-type policy

nodes.summary: Blobs complete before publish; reclaim under store lock, no reader pins
nodes.detail: Publication still verifies every reference resolves to a complete blob before the atomic state replacement, and unreferenced bytes are still reclaimed (the surviving core of 0029.04), now under the instance store lock. The host-only BlobScope and cross-process reader protection are withdrawn: blob lifetime assumes non-overlapping tool use, and concurrent read versus reclaim or clear is undefined.

realised.evidence: PR #215: PublishFetch checks all references under the instance lock before replacing state, then reclaims unreferenced blobs; acquisition-scoped cleanup on failure. The PR body says result/publication assertions were still being added

nodes.summary: Acquisition-only digestText fingerprints connector-chosen canonical payloads
nodes.detail: Capture-once connectors fingerprint their own canonical payload representation with digestText, which returns lowercase hex SHA-256 of each input's UTF-8 bytes in one batched request; nested BlobRef hashes participate. The capability is acquisition-only (never granted to captured readers) and the host implements it as a pure ContentDigest interpreter sharing blob storage's native SHA.

realised.evidence: PR #217 adds the batched native ContentDigest capability with a pure interpreter, used by Graph Mail fingerprints

editorial.note: String -> Text in BlobRef/BlobDownload/BlobResponse/readBlobText/FetchContext field types, following the SDK-wide packed Text transport owned by ADR 0007; no change to this lane's requirements

Swaps curation-register/acknowledgement vocabulary for recipe state following ADR 0014's redesign; the existing commitments (no retention of blobs, positions independent of recipe progress) are unchanged

Byte reads now travel in ADR 0007's raw body section instead of a binary-to-text codec in the string profile; the transport change is owned and recorded in lane 0007 (0007.21), and this lane's commitments (whole-blob reads, no author-visible base64) are unchanged

notes: This lane was born at seq 151 as a docs-only design. Its two halves fared very differently. The sync-position half (0029.06) was built within a day (seq 156) and then refined twice by implementation PRs that loosened the spec: config changes no longer invalidate a position, and an explicit --restart-sync was added. The blob half (0029.01-05: BlobRef, streamed downloads, scoped reads, reclamation and surface file paths) is the bulk of the ADR and is still entirely unrealised; no blob identifier ever reached code, and the position PRs explicitly defer blobs. The seq 155 String->Text sweep touches this lane only as a format follow-on, so I recorded it as editorial. Seq 164 (PR #212, docs-only) simplified the unbuilt blob half before any of it was implemented. Both changes withdraw something an earlier node stated, so they are replacements that restate the surviving core: 0029.09 replaces 0029.02 (no maxBytes or media-type policy), and 0029.10 replaces 0029.04 (BlobScope reader protection withdrawn in favour of a store lock and an explicit non-overlapping-use assumption). PR #214 at seq 166 lists 0029 as governing but implements only payload availability (ADR 0014) and explicitly defers blob storage, so no 0029 node is realised there. Seq 167 (PR #215) then built the whole blob half at once: BlobRef, host-streamed downloads, scoped captured reads, publication checks with reclamation, and CLI result paths, so 0029.01, 0029.03, 0029.05, 0029.09 and 0029.10 are realised there (0029.05 at medium confidence: paths are listed but not made read-only, and MCP is not separately evidenced). Its wording change moving byte reads onto ADR 0007's raw body is editorial here. Seq 168 (PR #217, Graph Mail) added payload fingerprints (0029.11), built in the same step.
